# Starter Merges
```{python}
import os
import pandas as pd

# =========================================================
# 1. Set working directory
# =========================================================
os.chdir(r"C:\Users\jtper\OneDrive\Documents\Capstone\project_data")

# =========================================================
# 2. Load files
# =========================================================
crime = pd.read_csv("state_crime.csv")
abortion = pd.read_csv("abortion_table.csv")
policy = pd.read_csv("abortion_policy_2000.csv")

unemp = pd.read_excel(
    "unemployment_data.xlsx",
    skiprows=7,
    names=[
        "fips",
        "state",
        "year",
        "civilian_noninstitutional_population",
        "civilian_labor_force_total",
        "labor_force_pct",
        "employment_total",
        "employment_pct",
        "unemployment_total",
        "unemployment_rate"
    ]
)

gdp = pd.read_csv("gdp_table.csv", skiprows=3)

# =========================================================
# 3. Clean column names
# =========================================================
for df_ in [crime, abortion, policy, unemp]:
    df_.columns = df_.columns.str.lower().str.strip()

gdp.columns = gdp.columns.str.strip()

# =========================================================
# 4. State name -> abbreviation map
# =========================================================
state_map = {
    "Alabama": "AL", "Alaska": "AK", "Arizona": "AZ", "Arkansas": "AR",
    "California": "CA", "Colorado": "CO", "Connecticut": "CT", "Delaware": "DE",
    "District of Columbia": "DC", "Florida": "FL", "Georgia": "GA", "Hawaii": "HI",
    "Idaho": "ID", "Illinois": "IL", "Indiana": "IN", "Iowa": "IA",
    "Kansas": "KS", "Kentucky": "KY", "Louisiana": "LA", "Maine": "ME",
    "Maryland": "MD", "Massachusetts": "MA", "Michigan": "MI", "Minnesota": "MN",
    "Mississippi": "MS", "Missouri": "MO", "Montana": "MT", "Nebraska": "NE",
    "Nevada": "NV", "New Hampshire": "NH", "New Jersey": "NJ", "New Mexico": "NM",
    "New York": "NY", "North Carolina": "NC", "North Dakota": "ND", "Ohio": "OH",
    "Oklahoma": "OK", "Oregon": "OR", "Pennsylvania": "PA", "Rhode Island": "RI",
    "South Carolina": "SC", "South Dakota": "SD", "Tennessee": "TN", "Texas": "TX",
    "Utah": "UT", "Vermont": "VT", "Virginia": "VA", "Washington": "WA",
    "West Virginia": "WV", "Wisconsin": "WI", "Wyoming": "WY"
}

# =========================================================
# 5. Clean abortion data
# =========================================================
abortion["state"] = abortion["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
abortion["year"] = pd.to_numeric(abortion["year"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")

# =========================================================
# 6. Clean crime data
#    Handles either abbreviations or full state names
# =========================================================
crime["state"] = crime["state"].astype(str).str.strip()
crime["state"] = crime["state"].replace(state_map).str.upper()
crime["year"] = pd.to_numeric(crime["year"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")

# =========================================================
# 7. Clean unemployment data
# =========================================================
unemp["state"] = (
    unemp["state"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
    .replace(state_map)
    .str.upper()
)

unemp["year"] = pd.to_numeric(unemp["year"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
unemp["unemployment_rate"] = pd.to_numeric(unemp["unemployment_rate"], errors="coerce")
unemp = unemp[unemp["state"].notna()].copy()

# =========================================================
# 8. Clean GDP data
# =========================================================
gdp = gdp[gdp["Description"] == "Current-dollar GDP (millions of current dollars)"].copy()
gdp = gdp.rename(columns={"GeoName": "state"})

year_cols = [col for col in gdp.columns if str(col).isdigit()]

gdp = gdp[["state"] + year_cols].melt(
    id_vars="state",
    value_vars=year_cols,
    var_name="year",
    value_name="gdp"
)

gdp["state"] = (
    gdp["state"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
    .replace(state_map)
    .str.upper()
)

gdp["year"] = pd.to_numeric(gdp["year"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
gdp["gdp"] = pd.to_numeric(gdp["gdp"], errors="coerce")
gdp = gdp[gdp["state"].isin(abortion["state"].unique())].copy()

# =========================================================
# 9. Clean policy data
# =========================================================
policy["state"] = (
    policy["state"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
    .replace(state_map)
    .str.upper()
)

policy = policy[["state", "policy_score"]].drop_duplicates()

# =========================================================
# 10. Diagnose key matching before merge
# =========================================================
print("Crime columns:")
print(crime.columns.tolist())

print("\nCrime head:")
print(crime.head())

print("\nAbortion states sample:")
print(sorted(abortion["state"].dropna().unique())[:10])

print("\nCrime states sample:")
print(sorted(crime["state"].dropna().unique())[:10])

print("\nAbortion years sample:")
print(sorted(abortion["year"].dropna().unique())[:10])

print("\nCrime years sample:")
print(sorted(crime["year"].dropna().unique())[:10])

ab_keys = abortion[["state", "year"]].drop_duplicates()
cr_keys = crime[["state", "year"]].drop_duplicates()

matches = ab_keys.merge(cr_keys, on=["state", "year"], how="inner")
print("\nAbortion keys:", ab_keys.shape[0])
print("Crime keys:", cr_keys.shape[0])
print("Matching keys:", matches.shape[0])

nonmatches = ab_keys.merge(cr_keys, on=["state", "year"], how="left", indicator=True)
print("\nSample unmatched abortion state-year pairs:")
print(nonmatches[nonmatches["_merge"] == "left_only"].head(20))

# =========================================================
# 11. Test crime merge only
# =========================================================
crime_cols_to_merge = [c for c in [
    "state",
    "year",
    "data.rates.violent.all",
    "data.rates.property.all",
    "data.rates.violent.murder",
    "data.rates.violent.rape",
    "data.rates.violent.robbery",
    "data.rates.violent.assault"
] if c in crime.columns]

test_merge = abortion.merge(
    crime[crime_cols_to_merge],
    on=["state", "year"],
    how="left"
)

print("\nCrime merge test head:")
print(test_merge.head())

if "data.rates.violent.all" in test_merge.columns:
    print("\nMissing share for violent crime after test merge:")
    print(test_merge["data.rates.violent.all"].isna().mean())

if "data.rates.property.all" in test_merge.columns:
    print("Missing share for property crime after test merge:")
    print(test_merge["data.rates.property.all"].isna().mean())

# =========================================================
# 12. Final merged Casey project panel
# =========================================================
df = abortion.merge(crime, on=["state", "year"], how="left")
df = df.merge(unemp, on=["state", "year"], how="left")
df = df.merge(gdp, on=["state", "year"], how="left")
df = df.merge(policy, on="state", how="left")

# =========================================================
# 13. Inspect final result
# =========================================================
print("\nFinal merged dataset shape:")
print(df.shape)

check_cols = [c for c in [
    "state",
    "year",
    "abortionratetotal",
    "data.rates.violent.all",
    "data.rates.property.all",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp",
    "policy_score"
] if c in df.columns]

print("\nPreview of key columns:")
print(df[check_cols].head(20))

print("\nMissingness in key columns:")
print(df[check_cols].isna().mean())
```

# Census Clean
```{python}
import os
import re
import pandas as pd

os.chdir(r"C:\Users\jtper\OneDrive\Documents\Capstone\project_data")

state_map = {
    "Alabama": "AL", "Alaska": "AK", "Arizona": "AZ", "Arkansas": "AR",
    "California": "CA", "Colorado": "CO", "Connecticut": "CT", "Delaware": "DE",
    "District of Columbia": "DC", "Florida": "FL", "Georgia": "GA", "Hawaii": "HI",
    "Idaho": "ID", "Illinois": "IL", "Indiana": "IN", "Iowa": "IA",
    "Kansas": "KS", "Kentucky": "KY", "Louisiana": "LA", "Maine": "ME",
    "Maryland": "MD", "Massachusetts": "MA", "Michigan": "MI", "Minnesota": "MN",
    "Mississippi": "MS", "Missouri": "MO", "Montana": "MT", "Nebraska": "NE",
    "Nevada": "NV", "New Hampshire": "NH", "New Jersey": "NJ", "New Mexico": "NM",
    "New York": "NY", "North Carolina": "NC", "North Dakota": "ND", "Ohio": "OH",
    "Oklahoma": "OK", "Oregon": "OR", "Pennsylvania": "PA", "Rhode Island": "RI",
    "South Carolina": "SC", "South Dakota": "SD", "Tennessee": "TN", "Texas": "TX",
    "Utah": "UT", "Vermont": "VT", "Virginia": "VA", "Washington": "WA",
    "West Virginia": "WV", "Wisconsin": "WI", "Wyoming": "WY"
}

def clean_col(x):
    x = str(x).strip().lower()
    x = x.replace("estimate!!", "")
    x = x.replace("margin of error!!", "moe_")
    x = x.replace("margin_of_error!!", "moe_")
    x = x.replace("percent!!", "pct_")
    x = x.replace("!!", "_")
    x = x.replace(" ", "_")
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    x = x.replace("-", "_")
    x = x.replace("/", "_")
    x = x.replace("(", "")
    x = x.replace(")", "")
    x = x.replace("'", "")
    x = x.replace(":", "")
    x = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "", x)
    x = re.sub(r"_+", "_", x).strip("_")
    return x if x else "unknown"

def make_unique(cols):
    counts = {}
    out = []
    for col in cols:
        if col not in counts:
            counts[col] = 0
            out.append(col)
        else:
            counts[col] += 1
            out.append(f"{col}_{counts[col]}")
    return out

acs_files = [
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2010.S0201-Data.csv", 2010),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2011.S0201-Data.csv", 2011),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2012.S0201-Data.csv", 2012),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2013.S0201-Data.csv", 2013),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2014.S0201-Data.csv", 2014),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2015.S0201-Data.csv", 2015),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2016.S0201-Data.csv", 2016),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2017.S0201-Data.csv", 2017),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2018.S0201-Data.csv", 2018),
    ("census_data/ACSSPP1Y2019.S0201-Data.csv", 2019),
]

acs_list = []

for file, year in acs_files:
    header_rows = pd.read_csv(file, header=None, nrows=2, low_memory=False)
    descriptive_names = [clean_col(x) for x in header_rows.iloc[1].fillna("")]
    descriptive_names = make_unique(descriptive_names)

    temp = pd.read_csv(file, skiprows=2, header=None, low_memory=False)
    temp.columns = descriptive_names

    # drop fully empty columns that often appear in ACS exports
    temp = temp.loc[:, ~temp.columns.str.match(r"^unknown(_\d+)?$")]

    possible_name_cols = [c for c in temp.columns if "name" in c]
    if not possible_name_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"No NAME-like column found in {file}. First 25 columns: {temp.columns.tolist()[:25]}")

    name_col = possible_name_cols[0]
    temp[name_col] = temp[name_col].astype(str).str.strip()

    temp = temp[temp[name_col].isin(state_map.keys())].copy()
    temp["state"] = temp[name_col].map(state_map)
    temp["year"] = year

    # ensure columns are unique again after filtering
    temp.columns = make_unique(temp.columns)

    acs_list.append(temp)

acs = pd.concat(acs_list, ignore_index=True, sort=False)

acs = acs.drop_duplicates(subset=["state", "year"])

for col in acs.columns:
    if col not in ["state", "year"] and "name" not in col:
        acs[col] = pd.to_numeric(acs[col], errors="coerce")

print("ACS shape:", acs.shape)
print(acs[["state", "year"]].head())
print(acs.columns.tolist()[:80])

df = df.merge(acs, on=["state", "year"], how="left")

print("Merged df shape after ACS:", df.shape)
print(df[["state", "year", "abortionratetotal", "unemployment_rate", "gdp", "policy_score"]].head(10))

```

# Simple and Robust Model
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# =====================================================
# 1. Start from your merged panel df
# =====================================================
df = df.copy()
df["state"] = df["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
df["year"] = pd.to_numeric(df["year"], errors="coerce")

# Choose crime outcome
crime_var = "data.rates.violent.all"
# crime_var = "data.rates.property.all"
# crime_var = "data.rates.violent.murder"

# Make sure core variables are numeric
base_numeric = [
    "abortionratetotal",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp",
    crime_var,
    "sex_and_age_18_to_24_years",
    "sex_and_age_25_to_34_years",
    "sex_and_age_35_to_44_years",
    "sex_and_age_45_to_54_years",
    "sex_and_age_male",
    "educational_attainment_high_school_graduate_or_higher",
    "educational_attainment_bachelors_degree_or_higher",
]
for col in base_numeric:
    if col in df.columns:
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

# =====================================================
# 2. Build cohort-style abortion exposure:
#    average abortion rate from 18 to 25 years earlier
# =====================================================
lag_frames = []

for lag in range(18, 26):
    temp = df[["state", "year", "abortionratetotal"]].copy()
    temp["year"] = temp["year"] + lag
    temp = temp.rename(columns={"abortionratetotal": f"abortion_lag_{lag}"})
    lag_frames.append(temp)

df_exposure = df.copy()
for temp in lag_frames:
    df_exposure = df_exposure.merge(temp, on=["state", "year"], how="left")

lag_cols = [f"abortion_lag_{lag}" for lag in range(18, 26)]

# Average exposure across the full 18–25 window
df_exposure["abortion_exposure_18_25"] = df_exposure[lag_cols].mean(axis=1)

# Optional: count how many lag years are actually observed
df_exposure["abortion_exposure_count"] = df_exposure[lag_cols].notna().sum(axis=1)

print("Non-missing broader-lag exposure:", df_exposure["abortion_exposure_18_25"].notna().sum())
print(df_exposure[["state", "year", "abortion_exposure_18_25", "abortion_exposure_count"]].head(30))

# =====================================================
# 3. Helper to run FE regression
# =====================================================
def run_fe_model(data, y_col, x_cols, cluster_col="state", min_exposure_count=None):
    needed = ["state", "year", y_col] + x_cols
    temp = data[needed].copy()

    if min_exposure_count is not None and "abortion_exposure_count" in data.columns:
        temp = temp.join(data["abortion_exposure_count"])
        temp = temp[temp["abortion_exposure_count"] >= min_exposure_count].copy()

    temp["state"] = temp["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
    temp["year"] = pd.to_numeric(temp["year"], errors="coerce")
    temp[y_col] = pd.to_numeric(temp[y_col], errors="coerce")

    for c in x_cols:
        temp[c] = pd.to_numeric(temp[c], errors="coerce")

    print("\nMissingness before dropna:")
    print(temp[needed].isna().mean().sort_values())

    temp = temp.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    print("Rows used after dropna:", temp.shape[0])

    if temp.empty:
        raise ValueError("No rows remain after dropna().")

    temp["year"] = temp["year"].astype(int)

    y = temp[y_col].to_numpy(dtype=float)

    X_main = temp[x_cols].astype(float).reset_index(drop=True)
    state_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["state"], prefix="state", drop_first=True, dtype=float).reset_index(drop=True)
    year_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["year"], prefix="year", drop_first=True, dtype=float).reset_index(drop=True)

    X = pd.concat([X_main, state_fe, year_fe], axis=1)
    X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant="add")

    model = sm.OLS(y, X.to_numpy(dtype=float)).fit(
        cov_type="cluster",
        cov_kwds={"groups": pd.Categorical(temp[cluster_col]).codes}
    )

    coef_table = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "coef": model.params[: len(x_cols) + 1],
            "pval": model.pvalues[: len(x_cols) + 1],
        },
        index=["const"] + x_cols,
    )

    return model, temp, coef_table

# =====================================================
# 4. MAIN MODEL
#    Full panel with cohort-style abortion exposure
# =====================================================
main_x = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp",
]

main_model, df_main_used, main_table = run_fe_model(
    df_exposure,
    crime_var,
    main_x,
    min_exposure_count=1
)

print("\nMAIN MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_main_used.shape)
print("\nMAIN MODEL KEY COEFFICIENTS")
print(main_table)
print("\nMAIN MODEL R-SQUARED:", main_model.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 5. ROBUST MODEL
#    2010–2019 with a reduced ACS set
#    Keep the ACS set modest so the sample survives
# =====================================================
robust_x = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp",
    "sex_and_age_18_to_24_years",
    "educational_attainment_bachelors_degree_or_higher",
]

df_robust = df_exposure[df_exposure["year"].between(2010, 2019)].copy()

robust_model, df_robust_used, robust_table = run_fe_model(
    df_robust,
    crime_var,
    robust_x,
    min_exposure_count=1
)

print("\nROBUST MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_robust_used.shape)
print("\nROBUST MODEL KEY COEFFICIENTS")
print(robust_table)
print("\nROBUST MODEL R-SQUARED:", robust_model.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 6. Compare core coefficients
# =====================================================
compare = pd.DataFrame({
    "main_coef": main_table["coef"].reindex(["abortion_exposure_18_25", "unemployment_rate", "gdp"]),
    "main_pval": main_table["pval"].reindex(["abortion_exposure_18_25", "unemployment_rate", "gdp"]),
    "robust_coef": robust_table["coef"].reindex(["abortion_exposure_18_25", "unemployment_rate", "gdp"]),
    "robust_pval": robust_table["pval"].reindex(["abortion_exposure_18_25", "unemployment_rate", "gdp"]),
})

print("\nCOMPARISON OF CORE COEFFICIENTS")
print(compare)

# =====================================================
# 7. Optional diagnostics
# =====================================================
print("\nExposure count distribution:")
print(df_exposure["abortion_exposure_count"].value_counts(dropna=False).sort_index())

print("\nSample of lag columns:")
print(df_exposure[["state", "year"] + lag_cols + ["abortion_exposure_18_25", "abortion_exposure_count"]].head(20))
```


# Weighted Model
```{python}
import statsmodels.api as sm
import pandas as pd

crime_var = "data.rates.violent.all"

# =====================================================
# 1. Prepare weighted dataset
# =====================================================
df_weighted = df_exposure.copy()

# keep only rows with at least some exposure
df_weighted = df_weighted[df_weighted["abortion_exposure_count"] >= 1].copy()

# define weights
df_weighted["weight"] = df_weighted["abortion_exposure_count"]

# =====================================================
# 2. Helper function for weighted FE model
# =====================================================
def run_weighted_fe_model(data, y_col, x_cols, weight_col, cluster_col="state"):
    needed = ["state", "year", y_col, weight_col] + x_cols
    temp = data[needed].copy()

    temp["state"] = temp["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
    temp["year"] = pd.to_numeric(temp["year"], errors="coerce")
    temp[y_col] = pd.to_numeric(temp[y_col], errors="coerce")

    for c in x_cols:
        temp[c] = pd.to_numeric(temp[c], errors="coerce")

    print("\nMissingness before dropna:")
    print(temp[needed].isna().mean().sort_values())

    temp = temp.dropna().copy()
    print("Rows used after dropna:", temp.shape[0])

    if temp.empty:
        raise ValueError("No rows remain after dropna().")

    temp["year"] = temp["year"].astype(int)

    y = temp[y_col].to_numpy(dtype=float)

    X_main = temp[x_cols].astype(float).reset_index(drop=True)
    state_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["state"], drop_first=True, dtype=float).reset_index(drop=True)
    year_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["year"], drop_first=True, dtype=float).reset_index(drop=True)

    X = pd.concat([X_main, state_fe, year_fe], axis=1)
    X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant="add")

    weights = temp[weight_col].to_numpy(dtype=float)

    # Weighted least squares
    model = sm.WLS(y, X.to_numpy(dtype=float), weights=weights).fit(
        cov_type="cluster",
        cov_kwds={"groups": pd.Categorical(temp[cluster_col]).codes}
    )

    coef_table = pd.DataFrame({
        "coef": model.params[:len(x_cols)+1],
        "pval": model.pvalues[:len(x_cols)+1]
    }, index=["const"] + x_cols)

    return model, temp, coef_table


# =====================================================
# 3. Run weighted main model
# =====================================================
xvars = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

weighted_model, df_w_used, weighted_table = run_weighted_fe_model(
    df_weighted,
    crime_var,
    xvars,
    weight_col="weight"
)

print("\nWEIGHTED MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_w_used.shape)
print("\nWEIGHTED MODEL RESULTS")
print(weighted_table)
print("\nWEIGHTED MODEL R-SQUARED:", weighted_model.rsquared)
```

# Policy Model
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# =====================================================
# 1. Prepare policy heterogeneity variables
# =====================================================

df_exposure = df_exposure.copy()

# Make sure policy_score is numeric
df_exposure["policy_score"] = pd.to_numeric(df_exposure["policy_score"], errors="coerce")

# Define high-policy states using the median policy score
median_policy = df_exposure["policy_score"].median()
print("Median policy score:", median_policy)

df_exposure["high_policy"] = df_exposure["policy_score"] > median_policy

# Optional check
policy_check = (
    df_exposure[["state", "policy_score", "high_policy"]]
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["state"])
    .sort_values("policy_score")
)
print("\nSTATE POLICY GROUPS (sample)")
print(policy_check.head(15))
print("\nNumber of high-policy states:",
      policy_check["high_policy"].sum())
print("Number of low-policy states:",
      (~policy_check["high_policy"]).sum())

# =====================================================
# 2. Define main regressors
# =====================================================

main_x = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

# =====================================================
# 3. Run model for HIGH-policy states
# =====================================================

df_high = df_exposure[df_exposure["high_policy"] == True].copy()

model_high, df_high_used, table_high = run_fe_model(
    df_high,
    crime_var,
    main_x,
    min_exposure_count=1
)

print("\nHIGH-POLICY MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_high_used.shape)
print("\nHIGH-POLICY MODEL RESULTS")
print(table_high)
print("\nHIGH-POLICY MODEL R-SQUARED:", model_high.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 4. Run model for LOW-policy states
# =====================================================

df_low = df_exposure[df_exposure["high_policy"] == False].copy()

model_low, df_low_used, table_low = run_fe_model(
    df_low,
    crime_var,
    main_x,
    min_exposure_count=1
)

print("\nLOW-POLICY MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_low_used.shape)
print("\nLOW-POLICY MODEL RESULTS")
print(table_low)
print("\nLOW-POLICY MODEL R-SQUARED:", model_low.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 5. Compare coefficients across groups
# =====================================================

hetero_compare = pd.DataFrame({
    "High Policy Coef": table_high["coef"].reindex(main_x),
    "High Policy pval": table_high["pval"].reindex(main_x),
    "Low Policy Coef": table_low["coef"].reindex(main_x),
    "Low Policy pval": table_low["pval"].reindex(main_x),
})

print("\nHETEROGENEITY COMPARISON")
print(hetero_compare)

# =====================================================
# 6. Interaction model in full sample
# =====================================================
# Note:
# Since policy_score is time-invariant, high_policy alone will be
# absorbed by state fixed effects in a standard FE setup.
# The interaction term is still identified because abortion exposure
# varies over time.

df_exposure["high_policy_int"] = df_exposure["high_policy"].astype(int)

df_exposure["abortionXhighpolicy"] = (
    df_exposure["abortion_exposure_18_25"] *
    df_exposure["high_policy_int"]
)

interaction_x = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "abortionXhighpolicy",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

interaction_model, df_int_used, interaction_table = run_fe_model(
    df_exposure,
    crime_var,
    interaction_x,
    min_exposure_count=1
)

print("\nINTERACTION MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_int_used.shape)
print("\nINTERACTION MODEL RESULTS")
print(interaction_table)
print("\nINTERACTION MODEL R-SQUARED:", interaction_model.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 7. Interpret interaction model
# =====================================================

base_coef = interaction_table.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"]
base_pval = interaction_table.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"]

diff_coef = interaction_table.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "coef"]
diff_pval = interaction_table.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "pval"]

high_effect = base_coef + diff_coef

print("\nINTERPRETATION OF INTERACTION MODEL")
print(f"Effect in LOW-policy states: {base_coef:.4f} (p={base_pval:.4f})")
print(f"Difference for HIGH-policy states: {diff_coef:.4f} (p={diff_pval:.4f})")
print(f"Implied effect in HIGH-policy states: {high_effect:.4f}")

# =====================================================
# 8. Optional summary table
# =====================================================

summary_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model": ["Low Policy", "High Policy", "Interaction: Low Baseline", "Interaction: High-Low Difference"],
    "Coefficient": [
        table_low.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        table_high.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        interaction_table.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        interaction_table.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "coef"]
    ],
    "P-value": [
        table_low.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        table_high.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        interaction_table.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        interaction_table.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "pval"]
    ]
})

print("\nSUMMARY OF HETEROGENEITY RESULTS")
print(summary_table)
```

# Table Creation
```{python}
def make_regression_table(models):
    rows_order = [
        "abortion_exposure_18_25",
        "unemployment_rate",
        "gdp",
        "sex_and_age_18_to_24_years",
        "educational_attainment_bachelors_degree_or_higher",
    ]

    labels = {
        "abortion_exposure_18_25": "Abortion exposure (18–25)",
        "unemployment_rate": "Unemployment rate",
        "gdp": "GDP",
        "sex_and_age_18_to_24_years": "Population age 18–24",
        "educational_attainment_bachelors_degree_or_higher": "Bachelor's+",
    }

    output = []

    for var in rows_order:
        coef_line = {"Variable": labels[var]}
        p_line = {"Variable": ""}
        
        for model_name, info in models.items():
            tab = info["table"]
            if var in tab.index:
                coef = tab.loc[var, "coef"]
                pval = tab.loc[var, "pval"]
                
                stars = ""
                if pval < 0.01:
                    stars = "***"
                elif pval < 0.05:
                    stars = "**"
                elif pval < 0.10:
                    stars = "*"
                
                coef_line[model_name] = f"{coef:.3f}{stars}"
                p_line[model_name] = f"({pval:.3f})"
            else:
                coef_line[model_name] = ""
                p_line[model_name] = ""
        
        output.append(coef_line)
        output.append(p_line)

    output.append({
        "Variable": "Observations",
        **{name: len(info["used_df"]) for name, info in models.items()}
    })
    output.append({
        "Variable": "R-squared",
        **{name: f"{info['model'].rsquared:.3f}" for name, info in models.items()}
    })
    output.append({
        "Variable": "State FE",
        **{name: "Yes" for name in models}
    })
    output.append({
        "Variable": "Year FE",
        **{name: "Yes" for name in models}
    })
    output.append({
        "Variable": "Clustered SE",
        **{name: "State" for name in models}
    })

    return pd.DataFrame(output)

models = {
    "Main": {
        "table": main_table,
        "model": main_model,
        "used_df": df_main_used
    },
    "Robust": {
        "table": robust_table,
        "model": robust_model,
        "used_df": df_robust_used
    },
    "Weighted": {
        "table": weighted_table,
        "model": weighted_model,
        "used_df": df_w_used
    }
}

final_table = make_regression_table(models)
final_table
```

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

crime_var = "data.rates.violent.all"

xvars = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

results = []

for state, g in df_exposure.groupby("state"):
    temp = g[["state", "year", crime_var] + xvars].copy()

    temp[crime_var] = pd.to_numeric(temp[crime_var], errors="coerce")
    for col in xvars:
        temp[col] = pd.to_numeric(temp[col], errors="coerce")

    temp = temp.dropna().copy()

    if temp.shape[0] < 5:
        continue

    year_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["year"], drop_first=True, dtype=float)
    X = pd.concat([temp[xvars], year_fe], axis=1)
    X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant="add")

    try:
        model = sm.OLS(temp[crime_var], X).fit()
        if "abortion_exposure_18_25" not in model.params:
            continue

        results.append({
            "state": state,
            "coef": model.params["abortion_exposure_18_25"],
            "pval": model.pvalues["abortion_exposure_18_25"],
            "n_obs": temp.shape[0]
        })
    except Exception:
        continue

state_coefs = pd.DataFrame(results)
state_coefs["state"] = state_coefs["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
state_coefs = state_coefs.dropna(subset=["coef"])
```

# Variable Assignment
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

crime_var = "data.rates.violent.all"

xvars = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

results = []

for state, g in df_exposure.groupby("state"):
    temp = g[["state", "year", crime_var, "policy_score"] + xvars].copy()

    temp[crime_var] = pd.to_numeric(temp[crime_var], errors="coerce")
    temp["policy_score"] = pd.to_numeric(temp["policy_score"], errors="coerce")

    for col in xvars:
        temp[col] = pd.to_numeric(temp[col], errors="coerce")

    temp = temp.dropna(subset=[crime_var] + xvars).copy()

    if temp.shape[0] < 5:
        continue

    year_fe = pd.get_dummies(temp["year"], drop_first=True, dtype=float)
    X = pd.concat([temp[xvars], year_fe], axis=1)
    X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant="add")

    try:
        model = sm.OLS(temp[crime_var], X).fit()

        if "abortion_exposure_18_25" not in model.params:
            continue

        policy_val = temp["policy_score"].dropna().iloc[0] if temp["policy_score"].notna().any() else None

        results.append({
            "state": state,
            "coef": model.params["abortion_exposure_18_25"],
            "pval": model.pvalues["abortion_exposure_18_25"],
            "n_obs": temp.shape[0],
            "policy_score": policy_val
        })

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{state} failed: {e}")
        continue

state_coefs = pd.DataFrame(results)
state_coefs["state"] = state_coefs["state"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
state_coefs = state_coefs.dropna(subset=["coef"])
```

# Table Function
```{python}
import pandas as pd

def make_model_table(coef_table, model, used_df, model_name="Model"):
    table = coef_table.copy()

    def stars(p):
        if p < 0.01:
            return "***"
        elif p < 0.05:
            return "**"
        elif p < 0.10:
            return "*"
        return ""

    rows = []
    for var in table.index:
        coef = table.loc[var, "coef"]
        pval = table.loc[var, "pval"]

        rows.append({
            "Variable": var,
            model_name: f"{coef:.3f}{stars(pval)}"
        })
        rows.append({
            "Variable": "",
            model_name: f"(p = {pval:.3f})"
        })

    rows.extend([
        {"Variable": "Observations", model_name: f"{len(used_df):,}"},
        {"Variable": "R-squared", model_name: f"{model.rsquared:.3f}"},
        {"Variable": "State FE", model_name: "Yes"},
        {"Variable": "Year FE", model_name: "Yes"},
        {"Variable": "Clustered SE", model_name: "State"},
    ])

    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    rename_dict = {
        "const": "Constant",
        "abortion_exposure_18_25": "Abortion exposure (18–25)",
        "abortion_exposure_std": "Abortion exposure (standardized)",
        "unemployment_rate": "Unemployment rate",
        "gdp": "GDP",
        "sex_and_age_18_to_24_years": "Population age 18–24",
        "educational_attainment_bachelors_degree_or_higher": "Bachelor's degree or higher",
        "abortionXhighpolicy": "Exposure × High-policy state"
    }

    out["Variable"] = out["Variable"].replace(rename_dict)

    styled = (
        out.style
        .hide(axis="index")
        .set_caption(model_name)
        .set_table_styles([
            {
                "selector": "caption",
                "props": [
                    ("caption-side", "top"),
                    ("font-size", "16px"),
                    ("font-weight", "bold"),
                    ("text-align", "left"),
                    ("padding", "8px 0")
                ]
            },
            {
                "selector": "th",
                "props": [
                    ("background-color", "#2f4f4f"),
                    ("color", "white"),
                    ("font-weight", "bold"),
                    ("text-align", "center"),
                    ("padding", "8px")
                ]
            },
            {
                "selector": "td",
                "props": [
                    ("padding", "6px 10px"),
                    ("border", "1px solid #d0d0d0")
                ]
            },
            {
                "selector": "table",
                "props": [
                    ("border-collapse", "collapse"),
                    ("width", "70%"),
                    ("font-family", "Arial, sans-serif"),
                    ("font-size", "13px")
                ]
            }
        ])
        .set_properties(subset=["Variable"], **{
            "text-align": "left",
            "font-weight": "normal"
        })
        .set_properties(subset=[model_name], **{
            "text-align": "right"
        })
        .apply(
            lambda row: [
                "background-color: #f7f7f7" if row.name % 2 == 0 else ""
                for _ in row
            ],
            axis=1
        )
    )

    return out, styled
```

# Weighted Hetero Models
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# =====================================================
# 1. Prepare weighted heterogeneity dataset
# =====================================================

df_hetero = df_exposure.copy()

# Make sure needed variables are numeric
df_hetero["policy_score"] = pd.to_numeric(df_hetero["policy_score"], errors="coerce")
df_hetero["abortion_exposure_count"] = pd.to_numeric(df_hetero["abortion_exposure_count"], errors="coerce")

# Keep only rows with at least some abortion exposure information
df_hetero = df_hetero[df_hetero["abortion_exposure_count"] >= 1].copy()

# Define weights based on number of observed lag years
df_hetero["weight"] = df_hetero["abortion_exposure_count"]

# =====================================================
# 2. Create high-policy indicator
# =====================================================

median_policy = df_hetero["policy_score"].median()
print("Median policy score:", median_policy)

df_hetero["high_policy"] = df_hetero["policy_score"] > median_policy
df_hetero["high_policy_int"] = df_hetero["high_policy"].astype(int)

# Optional state-level check
policy_check = (
    df_hetero[["state", "policy_score", "high_policy"]]
    .dropna()
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["state"])
    .sort_values("policy_score")
)

print("\nSTATE POLICY GROUPS (sample)")
print(policy_check.head(15))
print("\nNumber of high-policy states:", policy_check["high_policy"].sum())
print("Number of low-policy states:", (~policy_check["high_policy"]).sum())

# =====================================================
# 3. Define baseline regressors
# =====================================================

main_x = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

# =====================================================
# 4. Weighted model for HIGH-policy states
# =====================================================

df_high_w = df_hetero[df_hetero["high_policy"] == True].copy()

model_high_w, df_high_used_w, table_high_w = run_weighted_fe_model(
    df_high_w,
    crime_var,
    main_x,
    weight_col="weight"
)

print("\nHIGH-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_high_used_w.shape)
print("\nHIGH-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL RESULTS")
print(table_high_w)
print("\nHIGH-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL R-SQUARED:", model_high_w.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 5. Weighted model for LOW-policy states
# =====================================================

df_low_w = df_hetero[df_hetero["high_policy"] == False].copy()

model_low_w, df_low_used_w, table_low_w = run_weighted_fe_model(
    df_low_w,
    crime_var,
    main_x,
    weight_col="weight"
)

print("\nLOW-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_low_used_w.shape)
print("\nLOW-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL RESULTS")
print(table_low_w)
print("\nLOW-POLICY WEIGHTED MODEL R-SQUARED:", model_low_w.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 6. Compare weighted split-sample coefficients
# =====================================================

hetero_compare_w = pd.DataFrame({
    "High Policy Weighted Coef": table_high_w["coef"].reindex(main_x),
    "High Policy Weighted pval": table_high_w["pval"].reindex(main_x),
    "Low Policy Weighted Coef": table_low_w["coef"].reindex(main_x),
    "Low Policy Weighted pval": table_low_w["pval"].reindex(main_x),
})

print("\nWEIGHTED HETEROGENEITY COMPARISON")
print(hetero_compare_w)

# =====================================================
# 7. Weighted interaction model
# =====================================================
# high_policy itself is time-invariant and should NOT be included directly
# with state fixed effects. The interaction term is identified because
# abortion exposure varies over time.

df_hetero["abortionXhighpolicy"] = (
    df_hetero["abortion_exposure_18_25"] *
    df_hetero["high_policy_int"]
)

interaction_x_w = [
    "abortion_exposure_18_25",
    "abortionXhighpolicy",
    "unemployment_rate",
    "gdp"
]

interaction_model_w, df_int_used_w, interaction_table_w = run_weighted_fe_model(
    df_hetero,
    crime_var,
    interaction_x_w,
    weight_col="weight"
)

print("\nWEIGHTED INTERACTION MODEL SAMPLE SIZE:", df_int_used_w.shape)
print("\nWEIGHTED INTERACTION MODEL RESULTS")
print(interaction_table_w)
print("\nWEIGHTED INTERACTION MODEL R-SQUARED:", interaction_model_w.rsquared)

# =====================================================
# 8. Interpret weighted interaction model
# =====================================================

low_effect_w = interaction_table_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"]
low_pval_w = interaction_table_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"]

diff_effect_w = interaction_table_w.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "coef"]
diff_pval_w = interaction_table_w.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "pval"]

high_effect_w = low_effect_w + diff_effect_w

print("\nINTERPRETATION OF WEIGHTED INTERACTION MODEL")
print(f"Effect in LOW-policy states: {low_effect_w:.4f} (p={low_pval_w:.4f})")
print(f"Difference for HIGH-policy states: {diff_effect_w:.4f} (p={diff_pval_w:.4f})")
print(f"Implied effect in HIGH-policy states: {high_effect_w:.4f}")

# =====================================================
# 9. Summary table of weighted heterogeneity results
# =====================================================

summary_table_w = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model": [
        "Low Policy (Weighted)",
        "High Policy (Weighted)",
        "Interaction: Low Baseline (Weighted)",
        "Interaction: High-Low Difference (Weighted)"
    ],
    "Coefficient": [
        table_low_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        table_high_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        interaction_table_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "coef"],
        interaction_table_w.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "coef"]
    ],
    "P-value": [
        table_low_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        table_high_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        interaction_table_w.loc["abortion_exposure_18_25", "pval"],
        interaction_table_w.loc["abortionXhighpolicy", "pval"]
    ]
})

print("\nSUMMARY OF WEIGHTED HETEROGENEITY RESULTS")
print(summary_table_w)
```

# Coefficient Tree Chart
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def get_coef_ci(model, coef_table, var_name):
    coef = coef_table.loc[var_name, "coef"]
    param_order = list(coef_table.index)
    pos = param_order.index(var_name)
    se = model.bse[pos]
    lower = coef - 1.96 * se
    upper = coef + 1.96 * se
    return coef, lower, upper

results = []

model_specs = [
    ("Main", main_model, main_table),
    ("Robust", robust_model, robust_table),
    ("Weighted", weighted_model, weighted_table),
]

for name, model, table in model_specs:
    coef, lower, upper = get_coef_ci(model, table, "abortion_exposure_18_25")
    results.append({
        "Model": name,
        "coef": coef,
        "lower": lower,
        "upper": upper
    })

coef_df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print(coef_df)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
x = np.arange(len(coef_df))

plt.errorbar(
    x,
    coef_df["coef"],
    yerr=[
        coef_df["coef"] - coef_df["lower"],
        coef_df["upper"] - coef_df["coef"]
    ],
    fmt="o",
    capsize=5
)

for i, row in coef_df.iterrows():
    plt.text(i, row["coef"], f"{row['coef']:.2f}", ha="center", va="bottom")

plt.axhline(0, linestyle="--")
plt.xticks(x, coef_df["Model"])
plt.ylabel("Coefficient on Abortion Exposure")
plt.title("Abortion Exposure Coefficients with 95% Confidence Intervals")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Interaction Plots
```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ==========================================
# 1. Pull coefficients from interaction model
# ==========================================
# Assumes:
# position 1 = abortion_exposure_18_25
# position 2 = abortionXhighpolicy

b1 = interaction_model_w.params[1]
b2 = interaction_model_w.params[2]

# ==========================================
# 2. Pull variance-covariance matrix
# ==========================================
vcov = interaction_model_w.cov_params()

var_b1 = vcov[1, 1]
var_b2 = vcov[2, 2]
cov_b1b2 = vcov[1, 2]

# ==========================================
# 3. Compute effects
# ==========================================
# Low-policy effect
low_coef = b1
low_se = np.sqrt(var_b1)

# High-policy effect = baseline + interaction
high_coef = b1 + b2
high_var = var_b1 + var_b2 + 2 * cov_b1b2
high_se = np.sqrt(high_var)

# Difference = interaction term
diff_coef = b2
diff_se = np.sqrt(var_b2)

# ==========================================
# 4. Compute 95% confidence intervals
# ==========================================
low_lower = low_coef - 1.96 * low_se
low_upper = low_coef + 1.96 * low_se

high_lower = high_coef - 1.96 * high_se
high_upper = high_coef + 1.96 * high_se

diff_lower = diff_coef - 1.96 * diff_se
diff_upper = diff_coef + 1.96 * diff_se

# ==========================================
# 5. Put into dataframe
# ==========================================
coef_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Group": ["Low Policy", "High Policy", "Difference (High - Low)"],
    "coef": [low_coef, high_coef, diff_coef],
    "lower": [low_lower, high_lower, diff_lower],
    "upper": [low_upper, high_upper, diff_upper]
})

print(coef_df)

# ==========================================
# 6. Plot coefficient chart with 95% CIs
# ==========================================
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5))

x = np.arange(len(coef_df))

plt.errorbar(
    x,
    coef_df["coef"],
    yerr=[
        coef_df["coef"] - coef_df["lower"],
        coef_df["upper"] - coef_df["coef"]
    ],
    fmt="o",
    capsize=6
)

# Zero line
plt.axhline(0, linestyle="--")

# Labels
plt.xticks(x, coef_df["Group"])
plt.ylabel("Effect of Abortion Exposure on Crime")
plt.title("Interaction Model: Effects by Policy Environment")

# Add value labels
for i, row in coef_df.iterrows():
    va = "bottom" if row["coef"] >= 0 else "top"
    plt.text(i, row["coef"], f"{row['coef']:.2f}", ha="center", va=va)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
